meta: Dramas like My Love from Another Star: the Park Ji Eun blueprint, the leads who carry it, and where the rewrite got better.
standfirst: An alien four hundred years into his stay, a vain top actress next door, and twenty-one episodes that only needed seventeen. This is the rough draft of Crash Landing on You: same writer, same shape, less discipline, and a middle stretch that replays its own beats. Jun Ji Hyun is why it survived the decade, and Cheon Song Yi is still the best comic female lead in the catalog. The invented physics that gets the ending out of trouble is silly, and by then you will not care.

picks.why: The same writer, ten years of practice later. Park Ji Eun builds both the same way: an impossible gap between two people, a comic supporting bench doing real work, and a romance played completely straight underneath the jokes. This is the version where the middle holds and the side characters are as interesting as the leads. Difference: the obstacle is a border and a government instead of physics, so the danger is human and the ending has to be negotiated rather than invented.

Same writer, same lead actress, and close enough to be a remake. A creature out of her element, a con man in place of the actor, and Jun Ji Hyun doing a warmer version of the same register. Difference: the chemistry that carries this show is the exact thing Blue Sea is missing, and it runs four episodes longer than its idea, so the second half is padding with a past-life subplot attached.

Park Ji Eun's most recent, and Kim Soo Hyun's other career part. The same trick of hanging a huge emotional swing off jokes you did not think were load bearing, with a chaebol family in place of the alien premise. Difference: it starts with the marriage already collapsing, so it is heavy 4 grief work rather than a courtship, and the comedy has to fight for room.

The immortal and the mortal, done as tragedy instead of farce. Same central ache of a being who has outlived everyone and a woman with a normal lifespan, and the same willingness to spend a whole episode on two people talking. Difference: Goblin is built to hurt and its ending charges you for the four hundred years, where this one solves the gap with a shrug and a piece of pseudo-science.

Same director, same trick of a superpower used for small human problems. Oh Choong Hwan shoots romance like it is worth taking seriously, and the premonition premise gives every episode a clean job to do. Difference: it is a case-driven procedural at pace 4, so the plot never idles the way twenty-one episodes here have to.

Oh Choong Hwan again on a romance measured in centuries. A being who cannot age paired with somebody who will, plus the same appetite for a set piece and a costume change. Difference: the tone is guilt rather than comedy, the comic bench is thinner, and it ends bittersweet, which this show would never dare.

Fangirl devotion as the engine, which is exactly what Cheon Song Yi ran on. A woman whose whole interior life is organised around one famous man, played sincerely rather than mocked, and a time premise that keeps raising the price. Difference: it is 2024 and it moves, sixteen tight episodes with no slack middle and a loop that forces the plot forward every hour.

against.title: The Master's Sun
against.why: The default 2013 supernatural romcom to reach for next, and it runs on dread. Ghosts turn up to frighten, the comedy comes from panic rather than vanity, and the female lead is fragile where Cheon Song Yi is monstrous. The pleasure here is a woman with no shame at all, and this replaces her with somebody who needs protecting.

against.title: The Heirs
against.why: Paired with it because both were the 2013 event drama with the same wattage of cast. It is a high school class war with no jokes worth the name and a hero whose main activity is brooding at a staircase. Nothing in it is funny, and funny is the entire reason to watch this.

against.title: Boys Over Flowers
against.why: The classic gateway everyone gets handed, and it has aged three times worse than this has. The romance is built on wearing a woman down, the comedy is broad without being sharp, and there is no performance in it doing what Jun Ji Hyun does. Start somewhere else.
